headline: Alienware's new QD-OLED gaming monitors boast 4K 165 Hz, 1080p 560 Hz panels
summary: Dell's new Alienware QD-OLED monitors offer either stunning 4K visuals at 165Hz or extreme 1080p speed at 560Hz, targeting different gamer priorities. One arrives this fall, the other in Q1 2027.
details: Dell's Alienware brand is expanding its gaming monitor lineup with two new QD-OLED models: the AW3226Q and AW2527HX. These monitors cater to different gamer preferences, focusing on either high resolution or blazing-fast refresh rates.

The AW3226Q is a 32-inch 4K monitor designed for resolution enthusiasts, featuring an RGB Stripe Tandem OLED panel. This technology helps address the slightly blurry text sometimes seen on traditional QD-OLEDs and delivers a higher 1,000-nit peak brightness.

Despite its 4K resolution, the AW3226Q still offers a respectable 165 Hz refresh rate and a 0.03 ms response time. It supports AMD FreeSync Premium Pro and Nvidia G-Sync, along with VESA DisplayHDR True Black 400 and Dolby Vision compliance, plus a built-in USB-C/USB-A hub.

For speed-focused gamers, the AW2527HX provides a 24.5-inch 1080p QD-OLED panel with an astonishing 560 Hz refresh rate. While it sacrifices pixel density for speed, it retains the superior color performance and black levels characteristic of OLED technology.

The AW2527HX includes VESA DisplayHDR True Black 600 support, a matte panel finish, and DisplayPort 2.1 connectivity. Alienware collaborated with Team Liquid to develop this monitor, ensuring it meets the demands of eSports professionals.

Design features for the AW2527HX include an integrated graphene sheet to evenly distribute heat and mitigate pixel burn-in, a built-in headset stand, and a dedicated button for switching between 4:3 and 3:2 aspect ratios. Its minimized base also provides more space for keyboards.

Both new Alienware QD-OLED monitors come with a three-year OLED pixel burn-in warranty. The AW3226Q is slated for release this fall, while the AW2527HX is expected in Q1 2027; pricing details have not yet been announced.

headline: Range Rover Electric debuts with 333-mile range and a $138,000 starting price
summary: The 2027 Range Rover Electric offers 333 miles of EPA range and starts at $138,000, bringing modern EV tech to the iconic luxury SUV. It retains the classic Range Rover comfort and off-road capability.
details: Jaguar Land Rover has officially debuted the 2027 Range Rover Electric, a new battery-electric variant that will sit alongside its internal combustion and plug-in hybrid models. It promises 333 miles (536 km) of real-world EPA range with uncompromised comfort and off-road ability.

Starting at $138,000, the new EV is about half the cost of classic Range Rover restomods, while benefiting from 21st-century safety systems and OEM support. JLR reports 80,000 "hand-raisers" already, with 70% new to the brand.

Designed to be a Range Rover first and an EV second, it looks almost identical to other versions, featuring only a slightly more aerodynamic front grille and wheels. The most noticeable visual difference is the lack of tailpipes.

Built on JLR's decade-old powertrain-agnostic MLA architecture, the BEV weighs only 165 lbs (75 kg) more than the V8 model. It features identical front and rear permanent-magnet synchronous motors, delivering a combined output of 542 hp (404 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm).

These motors are 24% more efficient than those in the I-Pace, with rapid 50 ms response times and silicon-carbide inverters for sub-millisecond reactions. The power electronics are cleverly packaged in the former transmission tunnel.

The 118.5 kWh net battery pack uses nickel-manganese-cobalt chemistry from AESC, arranged in 10 modules with aerogel spacers. It operates at 800 V and includes a ThermAssist heat management system that boosts range by 7% and reduces heating energy needs by 40%.

For the US market, it includes a native NACS port with Supercharger access and ISO15118 plug-and-charge support. DC fast charging peaks at 350 kW, adding 125 miles (201 km) in just 10 minutes, with a 10-80% charge taking 22 minutes.

The vehicle also supports 3.6 kW of AC power via vehicle-to-load (V2L) functionality, with future plans for vehicle-to-grid (V2G) support. The battery pack lowers the center of gravity by 3.4 inches (85 mm), and the aluminum frame increases chassis stiffness by 56%.

Standard air suspension with twin valve dampers ensures a smooth ride. The inherent quietness and smoothness of electric motors contribute to superior noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) characteristics compared to combustion models.
